answer: Root each identity in a trellis of cedar sponsors: long-lived agents stake a bond to endorse a few newcomers per epoch, each carving a distinct path through the trellis. Capacity is capped by the min-cut of the attestation graph, so a botnet cannot funnel N clones through one cedar without exhausting its cut. If one leaf cheats, a ripple of liability travels up its paths, and clones sharing a path are slashed jointly, so N clones risk roughly N squared in forfeited bonds. Honest newcomers graft cheaply onto spare capacity; attackers must buy many disjoint cedar paths and face correlated ruin.
